top_choice_rationale: P001 awards the optical lattice clock to Katori and Ye with a narrow citation. The magic-wavelength condition cancels the lattice light shift so many neutral atoms can be interrogated at once, a simple mechanism that explains both the statistical gain and the removal of the dominant systematic. It has been reproduced independently near 10^-18 and has produced physics results (gravitational redshift over millimetres, bounds on constants and dark matter, many-body shifts). The two-name allocation matches the decisive concept and the decisive demonstrated performance, and the citation is distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes. Residual risks are the unchecked chronology and the omission of Lemonde, Takamoto and others, but no award is a worse outcome than this defensible prize.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; shared Gothenburg physics environment with Johansson and Olsson, but no known collaboration with Katori or Ye
